BonaLabs: migrate the website newsfeed to Discord
================================================

Prepared November 1, 2026. The owner confirmed DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN was added to
GitHub Actions secrets. Discord is selected locally in news-feed-settings.json.
Commit/push and the first successful Discord build/deploy are still pending.
Never store credentials in the settings file.

Approved server: 673917009897062411
Approved channels:
  https://discord.com/channels/673917009897062411/1164209144740458506
  https://discord.com/channels/673917009897062411/1354084517404737586

The owner requested recent existing publications as well as future announcements.
publish_from is therefore null. The collector reads the latest 100 messages per
channel, keeps the 12 newest eligible posts combined, and the Home displays 3.
Messages are ordered together by publication time. Identical announcements in
different channels remain separate posts; publish each announcement once.
Bots/webhooks and system messages are excluded by default. If announcements are
posted by a bot/webhook, review and set include_bots to true before activation.

SETUP

1. Create an application at https://discord.com/developers/applications (or use
   an existing bot you own). In Bot, enable Message Content Intent. Other
   privileged intents are unnecessary for this integration.

2. Install the bot in the approved server, with the bot scope and only View
   Channels + Read Message History. No Administrator or Send Messages permission
   is needed. In each of the two channel permission settings, ensure the bot
   can View Channel and Read Message History. Restrict its access to the news
   channels. Anyone reading the website will be able to see the copied content;
   use channels whose announcements are intended for public distribution.

3. Copy the bot token directly into a new GitHub Actions repository secret:
   Name: DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN
   https://github.com/BonaLabs/bonalabs.github.io/settings/secrets/actions
   Do not paste the token into chat, screenshots, the site, or a repository file.
   Do not reset an existing bot's token unless you also update its other users.

4. In .github/news-feed-settings.json source is already set to "discord".
   The server and both channel IDs are also configured. Keep the existing
   TELEGRAM_FEED_ENABLED=true repository variable: its historical name still
   gates the Pages workflow, including the Discord source. When source is
   discord, the collector makes no Telegram API calls.

5. Commit and push the migration files to main, including the new scripts,
   tests, assets/discord/.gitkeep, index.html and news-feed.js. Wait for the
   "BonaLabs news and Pages" workflow to complete build and deploy.

   IMPORTANT: the workflow file remains .github/workflows/telegram-news.yml.
   The cron-job.org URL, POST body and GitHub token can stay exactly as configured.
   The workflow display name changes; the dispatch URL does not.

6. Verify the Home displays recent Discord posts and Read on Discord links.
   Check two scheduled intervals without manual runs. Edits should update on
   the next successful sync, and deleted posts should disappear. API failures
   stop deployment and preserve the previous public feed. No permanent server
   or Gateway connection is used. The bot may appear offline in Discord.

7. After confirming the switch, the Telegram bot secret can be removed if no
   other integration uses it. Telegram invitation links and buttons have been
   removed from public pages; community panels now invite readers to Discord.

DETAILS

- The public snapshot is data/news-feed.json. Only Discord posts are displayed.
  There is no Telegram fallback. Its old snapshot, cached images and social icon
  are retained in the repository but excluded from the Pages package.
- A first Discord run with no eligible announcements fails rather than clearing
  the Telegram feed: verify permissions, channel selection and include_bots.
- Each successful run reconstructs the recent feed, reflecting edits/deletions.
  If a channel returns an empty history, previously published messages are
  checked individually. Only Unknown Message (404/code 10008) counts as deleted;
  revoked permissions, missing channels and service errors preserve the feed.
- IDs remain strings throughout to avoid JavaScript rounding Discord snowflakes.
- Attached JPG/PNG/WebP/GIF images up to 8 MiB are cached under assets/discord;
  signed Discord CDN URLs are not exposed. Spoiler attachments are skipped.
  Video/files/stickers are accessed through the original Discord message link.
- Text and basic formatting are normalized to safe plain text. Raw author data,
  roles, tokens and full API payloads are never written to the public snapshot.
- Source message links require Discord access. The site's copies need no login.
- Native GitHub cron remains a fallback. Neither scheduler nor runner latency
  guarantees an exact 15-minute publication deadline. Open Home tabs refresh
  their snapshot every five minutes.

CHECKS (offline; never run a live collector locally while Actions is active)

  python -m unittest discover -s .github/tests -v
  node --check news-feed.js

References:
https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message#get-channel-messages
https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/gateway#message-content-intent
https://docs.discord.com/developers/reference#signed-attachment-cdn-urls
